Comment:
As an ML engineer working in industry, I welcome the EU’s new framework as a much-needed step toward accountable AI deployment. The risk-based approach helps focus attention where harm is most likely, and the emphasis on transparency, documentation, and human oversight will push companies to adopt better engineering and governance practices. That said, a few cautions: (1) Compliance must be practical — overly prescriptive requirements for low-risk systems could stifle innovation and impose disproportionate costs on smaller firms; (2) Harmonization with other jurisdictions and clarity on cross-border data flows will be critical to avoid fragmentation; and (3) Regulators should support standards, tooling, and clear templates (model cards, evaluation protocols) so organizations can comply without reinventing the wheel. Ultimately, the framework is a positive catalyst, but success will depend on balanced enforcement, industry collaboration, and investment in developer-friendly compliance tools.
